payload.claim: Criterion 4 requires `run_stack_batch` to ask `stack_base_alive` "before the mint," but the witness `test_a_stack_whose_base_branch_is_gone_refuses_its_order_without_an_abort` never exercises this ordering: every arrangement in it calls `run_stack_batch` with `review=None`, so the `if review is not None:` mint block at line 564 is always skipped regardless of where the stack-base check sits relative to it. Swapping the two blocks so the mint runs first and the stack-base-gone check runs second produces identical behaviour under every scenario the witness drives (all four `stack_base_alive` arrangements still pass), yet it violates the stated criterion: a spec whose stack base turned out to be gone would now be minted (a wasted ledger task and `attach_run_to_batch`) before being refused, contradicting "Nothing more is minted, reviewed or run." No other test combines a live `review`/`mint` with a non-`None` `stack_base_alive`, so this ordering is unverified.
